member.name: T:FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.ColumnEvaluator
member.summary: The two rules per column (trecho) of the attempt record, new in gla-02: the traced level (trace, open point 1) and the accuracy per column (correct, open point 8).

remarks.para: Pass the final path, in the order the points were recorded (after the game's SignalPath.FinalizePath on arrival and death). The rules do not assume increasing x: the game's path has two exceptions of up to one frame, a point ahead of a vertical (gravity flipped while going back) and a final point behind the previous one (collision while going back).

Column with trace. Column i has trace when the path has at least one point and the x of its last point is greater than origin + i, strictly. Both rules use this condition, so trace[i] and correct[i] are null in exactly the same columns, as the attempt record validator requires, and the traced columns are a prefix. A path that ends exactly at the left border of column i does not reach it.
The final clock edge, at x = n in the slack, belongs to no column: what the path does in the slack does not enter these rules (it enters ).

member.name: M:FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.ColumnEvaluator.TraceLevels(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.PathPoint},System.Int32,FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.PhaseGeometry)
member.summary: The traced level of each column (0, 1 or null): the level of the path at 3/4 of the column (origin + i + 0.75, the center of its second half, the same split in half columns as the simulation).
member.remarks: Going through the points in the order of the path, the level at the sample point is the level of the last point with x <= sample. On a vertical exactly at the sample point, it is the point after the vertical. If the path ends inside the column before the sample point, it is the level of the last point. The level of a point is 1 when its y is closer to the y of level 1 than to the y of level 0. Columns without trace are null. If no point has x <= sample (a path that starts after the sample point, which the game does not produce), it is the level of the first point.
member.param: The final path.
The number of columns of the phase.
The geometry; null for .

member.name: M:FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.ColumnEvaluator.Correctness(FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.AnswerKeyCorners,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.PathPoint})
member.summary: The accuracy of each column (1, 0 or null), by the green or red criterion of the game ().

remarks.para: Each piece of the path between consecutive points is cut at the borders of the columns [origin + i, origin + i + 1), using its smallest and largest x (it may go backwards); a part keeps the original ends of the piece where they are inside the column. A vertical piece belongs to the column that contains its x. Each part is checked against the corners: the column is 1 when all its parts are valid and 0 when some part is invalid. Columns without trace are null.

Unlike the drawing on the screen, a long piece (a dash, for example) that crosses a column border is not all red when each cut part fits a band: only the part that is out of the band counts. Parts before column 0 and in the slack are not evaluated. A column with trace but no part (only when the path starts after it, which the game does not produce) is 1.

member.param: The answer key corners of the phase, with their geometry.
The final path.

member.name: T:FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.JkSimulator
member.summary: The J-K flip-flop of the game, ported from FlipFlopSimulator.SimulateJK (v0.15.0) without change of behavior.
member.remarks:
Q starts at 0.
The clock edges are at the start of the columns multiple of 6, from column 6 on, up to column n inclusive (the edge in the slack). At an edge, J and K are sampled in the previous column: J = 1 and K = 0 sets Q, J = 0 and K = 1 resets it, J = K = 1 toggles it, J = K = 0 keeps it.
The edge is ignored when Preset or Clear was active in the previous column.
Preset or Clear active in a column changes Q in the second half of that column.
The active edge of the clock does not change the simulation, as in the game.

member.name: T:FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.PhaseDefinition
member.summary: The logical part of a phase of the game: name, clock cycles, flip-flop type, active edge, input signals and active level of the asynchronous signals. Colors, description, floor, ceiling and obstacles are not part of it.

remarks.para: The library reads no phase file: each consumer builds the definition with its own reader (the game with its LevelData, the API and the synthetic data script with the reader of gla-07), using for the signals. The rules of the file (the legacy name clockCicles, asyncActive as "low", "high", 0 or 1, with high as the default) stay with the reader.

The signals may be longer than the number of columns and have different lengths, as in the files of the game. J and K read beyond their end are 0. Preset and Clear missing, empty or read beyond their end are inactive, whatever the active level, as in the game.
The definition is immutable: the signal arrays are copied.

member.name: T:FlipNflop.Commons.PhaseRules.SegmentValidator
member.summary: The green or red criterion of the game for a piece of the path, ported from PathVerifier.IsSegmentValid (v0.15.0) without change of behavior.
member.remarks:
A piece is valid (green) when both its ends fit the band of one same segment of the answer key. The orientation that decides is the one of the answer key segment, not of the piece:
a level segment (its corners differ in y by at most 0.1): y of both ends within the tolerance of the level, and x within the segment with a margin of 0.1;
a transition segment: x of both ends within the tolerance of the x of the transition, and y within the segment with a margin of 0.1. So, next to a transition, a horizontal piece on either level is valid, and a switch early or late by up to the tolerance stays all green.
A piece shorter than 0.01 is valid. The others are invalid (red).
